Q1.problem_type_and_essence: precedence-constrained DAG scheduling to minimize peak live-buffer residency under L0 exclusivity constraints

input_target_constraints.input: DAG nodes/edges with Op, Type, Size and dependency relationships

baseline.name: Kahn topological list scheduling with FREE-first + critical-path/slack tie-break
six_hour_plan: maintain ready set and prefer legal FREE nodes
tie-break computation nodes by critical-path/slack and ALLOC by incremental peak cost
replay Cmax and all constraints on six workloads
baseline.why: simple, deterministic, easy to debug, O((N+E)logN) with a heap, and provides a fair floor before metaheuristics

author_route.method: type-priority greedy initialization + tabu/neighborhood search using swap/insert/reverse
why_fit: local moves can improve buffer lifetime overlap
tabu search is a natural non-gradient optimizer for discrete schedules
author_route.evidence_boundary: paper claims size and criticality terms and adaptive tabu length, but appendix greedy code only uses coarse Op-type scores and fixed tabu_length=20

major_alternatives.why_can_work: same discrete feasible-order search and already available in same case group
major_alternatives.when_prefer: when matched-budget experiments show better Cmax or better robustness across seeds

major_alternatives.why_can_work: can provide exact/near-exact gap for validating heuristic quality
major_alternatives.when_prefer: small or compressed DAGs where exact solve is tractable

major_alternatives.model: beam search / A* with admissible or problem-specific lower bound
major_alternatives.why_can_work: keeps multiple promising partial topological orders and can exploit peak-memory lower bounds
major_alternatives.when_prefer: medium graphs when deterministic quality is more valuable than stochastic search

not_recommended.why_not_now: no large training distribution of graph instances and no evidence that policy training beats simple graph heuristics under contest time budget
wastes search on topologically invalid schedules unless feasibility-preserving encoding/repair dominates runtime

switch_conditions: use CP-SAT exact gap on small sampled subgraphs to calibrate heuristic quality
retain tabu only if it beats the six-hour baseline and S025 SA under matched evaluation budget and multiple seeds
if local feasible move generation rate collapses on large DAGs, switch to partial-order-aware insertion/beam search

Q2.problem_type_and_essence: interval/lifetime-aware multi-cache address allocation with spill decisions minimizing extra DDR movement under capacity and non-overlap constraints

input_target_constraints.input: Q1 schedule + buffer lifetimes/sizes/types + cache capacities + COPY_IN usage
input_target_constraints.objective: minimize extra data movement; runtime is secondary only if explicitly normalized/lexicographically handled

baseline.name: lifetime sweep + Best-Fit allocator + deterministic spill victim by incremental transfer cost and next-use distance
six_hour_plan: build buffer lifetimes from fixed Q1 schedule
allocate each cache with Best-Fit/free-list sweep
on overflow choose legal victim with lowest true incremental spill bytes, tie-break by farthest next use
replay capacity/non-overlap and exact extra-transfer metric
baseline.why: transparent and produces a strong deterministic baseline before population metaheuristics

author_route.method: paper-labeled ABQPSO with sequence/offset/spill mixed encoding + repair + local search
why_fit: repair operators can enforce hard cache constraints
population search can explore spill/address interactions
author_route.evidence_boundary: appendix has a long Q2 MATLAB listing, but Mbest and local attractor P are computed and never used; update equations are velocity-style PSO, so the claimed quantum-behaved mechanism is not implementation-verified

major_alternatives.why_can_work: address/spill decisions can be exact benchmarks and produce optimality gaps
reported transfer is much lower on all six workloads, although common-evaluator verification is still required
major_alternatives.when_prefer: when same evaluator confirms lower transfer with valid constraints

major_alternatives.model: simulated annealing / large-neighborhood search around deterministic allocator
major_alternatives.why_can_work: keeps a feasible allocator as decoder and searches only spill/victim decisions
major_alternatives.when_prefer: when direct mixed-code population search is too expensive

not_recommended.model: raw scalarized Bytes + Cycles without normalization
not_recommended.why_not_now: units and magnitudes are incomparable; 0.1*Cycles can dominate the primary Bytes objective unpredictably

not_recommended.model: ABQPSO name without active quantum update
not_recommended.why_not_now: algorithm label does not justify extra complexity when its defining Mbest/P terms are dead in the visible implementation

switch_conditions: keep population metaheuristic only after common-evaluator comparison against deterministic Best-Fit and S025 route
use lexicographic optimization or normalized epsilon constraint if runtime is truly secondary
if QPSO is retained, implement and test the actual quantum position-update primitive and ablate it

Q3.problem_type_and_essence: resource-constrained multi-objective scheduling: reduce makespan while keeping extra data movement within the problem-defined hard tolerance

input_target_constraints.input: feasible Q2 schedule/allocation/spill plan + node cycles/pipes/dependencies
hard_constraints: official transfer-tolerance cap must be explicit before Pareto ranking

baseline.name: epsilon-constraint local search from Q2 feasible solution
six_hour_plan: set transfer <= 1.05*C2 as hard feasibility gate
use critical-path/earliest-start resource-aware list scheduling to reduce makespan
perform small topology-preserving local moves and accept only feasible improvements
report feasible Pareto/operating points and exact replay
baseline.why: matches the contest requirement that transfer cannot significantly increase and avoids returning attractive but infeasible Pareto points

author_route.method: DPEA dual-population multi-objective evolutionary algorithm with LHS initialization, nondominated sorting, crowding and external archive
why_fit: dual populations conceptually separate convergence and exploration
author_route.evidence_boundary: DPEA is described only in prose/pseudocode; Appendix A contains no Q3 implementation. Eq.6.67 also changes the spill-cost semantics from Q2 by assigning zero cost to COPY_IN-used spills.

major_alternatives.model: NSGA-II / MOEA-D with explicit feasibility-first rules
major_alternatives.when_prefer: when multiple trade-off points are genuinely required

major_alternatives.why_can_work: directly encodes the hard transfer cap and minimizes runtime
major_alternatives.when_prefer: when contest statement prioritizes runtime under a fixed transfer tolerance

major_alternatives.model: resource-constrained critical-path scheduling + deterministic spill allocator
major_alternatives.why_can_work: strong six-hour baseline with clear causal relation to makespan

not_recommended.model: unconstrained Pareto optimization without the transfer cap
not_recommended.why_not_now: a hard contest constraint must be enforced before dominance ranking
a radar plot of before/after metrics does not demonstrate nondominance, diversity or operating-point selection

switch_conditions: DPEA enters the mainline only when executable implementation exists and feasible nondominated fronts beat NSGA-II/epsilon baseline under matched budgets
if only one final operating point is required, prefer epsilon-constraint over a complex MOEA
reconcile Eq.6.67 to the Q2 spill-cost definition before any Q3 metric is trusted
